method.decisionRule: A green authored checker is checker-scope evidence only. Acceptance required independent source projection reconstruction and falsification probes outside the authored fixture set.
method.sourceReconstruction: Parsed the exact pinned OPERABILITY v2 bytes with duplicate-key rejection and independently selected the declared REQUEST-ID-V1 paths without importing the candidate checker.
method.capabilityReview: After independently verifying all four hashes, imported the candidate checker as the system under test and exercised its model directly rather than trusting its aggregate positive/negative booleans.
method.trustOrderingReview: Used isolated temporary copies and side-effect markers. One probe changed source bytes and confirmed rejection before source import; a second retained the exact pinned source bytes while supplying a timestamp-valid cached bytecode image for the same module.
method.normalCheckerUse: Normal and selftest runs were recorded only as the behavior of the authored checker and were not treated as independent acceptance.

blockingFindings.finding: The checker hashes check-operability.py and then asks Python's SourceFileLoader to import that path. SourceFileLoader may execute a timestamp-valid __pycache__ image instead of compiling the verified source bytes. sys.dont_write_bytecode prevents cache writes, not cache reads.

setup: Copy the four frozen inputs to an isolated temporary directory.
Leave check-operability.py byte-identical at its pinned SHA-256.

Create a timestamp-based check-operability cache image whose header matches the exact source mtime and size, but whose code writes a marker and exposes only the expected BINDING and callable check API.
Run the exact TrustedRequestContext checker with python3 -B.
counterexample.observed: The marker contained PYC_EXECUTED, the checker exited 0, and it reported the candidate green while check-operability.py still had the exact pinned hash.

blockingFindings.consequence: The bytes executed as the pinned source checker are not the bytes whose hash was verified. An unpinned or stale cache image can execute arbitrary import-time behavior and satisfy the shallow BINDING/check API test, so TRC-1 and the declared hash-before-import boundary are not established.
requiredRepair: Execute only the exact byte buffer that was hashed: read once, hash that buffer, decode/compile that buffer and execute the resulting code object in a fresh module namespace without importlib cache selection.
Alternatively avoid executable import entirely if the leaf needs only a binding declaration that can be checked without execution.
Add an isolated regression containing a source-hash-clean, timestamp-valid malicious pyc and require rejection with no side effect.
Do not treat PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, sys.dont_write_bytecode or deleting a current cache as a durable repair; none prevents a future cache read.

blockingFindings.finding: The executable design oracle checks only isinstance at projection time and models foreign construction only by calling the constructor with an unequal token. A caller can bypass __init__ with object.__new__, set the name-mangled request-id slot, and obtain an object that _request_id accepts. The module-level _MINT_TOKEN also directly constructs contexts and is itself accepted by pickle, despite the exact tokenRule saying the token is nonserializable.

counterexamples.probe: object.__new__(_TrustedRequestContextV1), object.__setattr__ of _TrustedRequestContextV1__request_id to req1_ab repeated, then _request_id

counterexamples.observed: accepted as 37 bytes; the round-tripped object loses identity and is rejected, but serialization itself did not reject

blockingFindings.consequence: The prose remains implementable in Rust and the production-runtime residual is honest, but the authored checker cannot be cited as exercising or falsifying ingress-only capability provenance. Its green capability controls overstate what the model checks.
requiredRepair: Either strengthen the executable oracle so projection validates ingress-established provenance and the private token rejects serialization, with explicit object.__new__, leaked-token and token-roundtrip probes, or narrow the checker evidence claim to API-shape illustration and explicitly exclude same-process reflective construction from TRC-2 through TRC-4.
Keep PRODUCTION-CAPABILITY-IMPLEMENTATION open after either repair; a Python model cannot demonstrate the Rust visibility boundary, allocator, registry, restart or concurrency implementation.
Add retained negative fixtures for every construction route the successor claims to exclude, rather than routing all origins through one authored wrong-token helper.

confirmedProperties.note: The candidate sourceProjection is byte-semantically equal to an independent reconstruction from the exact pinned OPERABILITY v2 REQUEST-ID-V1 paths.
The normal mint path accepts lowercase req1_ plus exactly 32 hexadecimal characters and rejects uppercase and UUID aliases.
Raw text and parsed JSON cannot satisfy the normal projection boundary.
Internal retry preserves object identity and reservation count; distinct API and recovery invocations obtain distinct contexts; duplicate candidates and prior-context reuse are rejected.
Independent malformed parsed shapes returned findings without exceptions and a nested duplicate key was rejected.
The reviewed leaf names and opens only itself and the pinned OPERABILITY v2 pair. It does not load EventEnvelope, E8, OP6 or a current OPERABILITY successor.

retainedResiduals.effect: No Rust visibility boundary, allocator, durable/process registry, restart behavior, collision injection, or concurrency implementation has been demonstrated. This residual survives any checker repair.
The checker models a single-process set update; it is not evidence of a durable atomic unique constraint, eight-candidate allocator, I/O failure handling or multi-thread/process behavior.
This leaf normatively excludes RequestId and intentionally defines no downstream semantic schema. It does not independently promote E8, OP6, Evidence or current OPERABILITY.
